title: Latino Museum Gets a Home on the National Mall
summary:
For six years, the National Museum of the American Latino has not had a building of its own. Soon it will.

In August, the leaders of the Smithsonian voted to give the museum a permanent home in the Arts and Industries Building. This 145-year-old building is on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. Because the Smithsonian already owns it, the museum does not need Congress to approve a new site. President Trump has criticized the Smithsonian, and using a building it already owns avoids a possible political fight.

Jorge Zamanillo is the museum's founding director. He said people worked for more than 30 years to create the museum, with support from both political parties. A law creating it was passed in December 2020.

The building opened in 1881 as the Smithsonian's first national museum. Now it will be home to its newest one. Zamanillo said the museum will share many different stories about Latinos in American history.
why_it_matters: Kids who visit Washington, D.C., will be able to learn many stories about Latinos in American history in one place.
